claims.text: This filing is the driver's, and it asks for the 5.00 SGD to be put back into the driver's hands. The payments ledger already records that money with the rider — payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, cancelled_fee 5.00 — and the trip record shows the fee reversed at 07:59:40, refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver. Read off the record, the disposition that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is that this present state stand: POL-GEN-03 defines NO_ACTION as party-relative — the filing party's claim not being supported and the present state standing — and it never means 'restore a charge'; POL-NS-22's licence list itself contains NO_ACTION for the case where the fee does not stand. A ruling that re-charges the rider here would have to displace a state the platform itself created after reviewing the rider's complaint, and the record does not do that.

No artifact in this package carries the fact a no-show charge presupposes — that the rider did not come to the pickup. EV-GPS-05058 is a driver-device trace and its rider_track is empty: there is no rider-side presence data at all, so nothing shows where the rider was between 07:39:30 and the 07:51:40 cancellation, and every derived fact in that artifact (fix count, arrival corroboration, the stationary dwell) is driver-side. The rider's account that she was in the building is met by the driver's own account that he came early, which the record confirms: arrived_at 07:39:30 against a 07:45:00 booking. The question of whether the rider was absent within the free wait is therefore open on the evidence. POL-NS-26 makes a no-show ruling final, so the only route to a human on this record is POL-GEN-26: a fact the rule needs that the evidence cannot establish sends the case to a reviewer with the open question stated, rather than charging the rider on it.

The record's own wait machinery ran against the rider's booked time, not her conduct. The free-wait timer started at the driver's early arrival (07:39:35) and expired at 07:44:35 — twenty-five seconds before the 07:45:00 pickup the rider had booked — and the platform applied the 5.00 SGD fee line within four seconds of the cancellation (07:51:44). POL-NS-21 measures a scheduled trip's free wait from the scheduled pickup time where the driver arrived before it, which is exactly this case, so the timer that produced this charge departed from the clause and treated the rider as late before her own booked time had arrived. A charge generated on that footing is not one the rider should be made to carry, and on a record whose no-show process ran early the conservative reading is the one POL-GEN-26 requires.

The rider does not contend that the driver breached the contact obligation or missed the arrival deadline, and I will not stretch the record to say otherwise. EV-CHAT-05058 carries two driver messages (07:40:00 and 07:46:20) and EV-TRIP-05058 two unanswered in-app calls (07:47:30 and 07:50:10), all timestamped before the 07:51:40 cancellation, so POL-NS-23's obligation is met on the face of these artifacts and the derived obligation_met flag is true; and the 07:39:30 arrival is comfortably before POL-NS-24's 07:50:00 deadline. The rider's case is therefore not that the driver failed those steps, but that nothing in this package establishes the rider's absence on which the fee depends.

claims.text: The free wait was served in full. The trip was scheduled for 07:45 and the driver reached the pickup at 07:39:30, so under POL-NS-21 the wait runs from the scheduled time (07:45) and expires at 07:50; the driver cancelled at 07:51:40, and the trip record's own derived free_wait block returns cancelled_after_free_wait = true with 400 s from the wait's start to the cancellation. The driver in fact waited past even the platform's own short timer, which expired at 07:44:35.

The arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, as POL-NS-21's arrival test requires. The nearest fix to the pickup point sits 1.76 m away at 07:40:40 with a reported accuracy of 3 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace's derived arrival_check returns corroborated = true with accuracy_reported = true. The trace itself is clean: 47 fixes at 30 s intervals from 07:28:40 to 07:51:40, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 30 s, far under the 120 s policy impairment threshold.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is satisfied on its own terms, so the fee is not voided on that ground. The record shows two in-app chat messages sent by the driver (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and two in-app calls placed by the driver (07:47:30, unanswered, rang 28 s; 07:50:10, unanswered, rang 20 s) — every one of them before the 07:51:40 cancellation. The derived contact_before_cancel block returns obligation_met = true with call_count 2 and message_count 2.

The rider has no counter-ground under POL-NS-24. The driver-no-show deadline is scheduled 07:45 plus 5 minutes, i.e. 07:50, and the driver was at the pickup from 07:39:30, so arrived_by_deadline is true; there is neither a full refund on that clause nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit, which requires both a late arrival and a failure to attempt contact — and contact was attempted twice.

With the wait, the arrival and the contact obligation all met, the conditions of POL-NS-22 are made out and the 5.00 SGD fee belongs to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The amount charged is exactly the policy fee — fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy = true — so no fee-amount referral arises either, and POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, 5.00 SGD each.

The 07:59:40 ledger entry is an interim reversal 'pending review', not a determination of this dispute: the ledger still reads payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00, and the 5.00 SGD was withheld from the driver. That is why the party-relative reading of POL-GEN-03 matters — NO_ACTION means the present state stands, and here the present state leaves the refunded 5.00 with the rider and nothing with the driver. Reading the outcome off the record, the driver's claim is vindicated only by DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

The rider's answer — that the driver arrived early and therefore the cancellation was not her fault — is no answer under the policy. POL-NS-21 anchors the free wait to scheduled_at precisely in the case where the driver arrives before the scheduled time, so an early arrival neither shortens the wait the driver owes nor excuses a rider who is not present; and on the rider's own statement she came down at 07:53, after the 07:51:40 cancellation and after the 07:50 expiry of the wait.

Nothing in the GPS evidence places the rider at the pickup at any time before the cancellation: the trace carries an empty rider_track, so her account that she came down at 07:53 is uncorroborated assertion, and the only fact it could support — a driver no-show under POL-NS-24 — fails on the arrival and contact record in any event.

Disclosure as POL-GEN-02 requires: EV-ADVIS-05058-01 is a MISSING artifact, impairs at weight 0.0, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and has no payload, so it carries no fact either way. Its absence does not open POL-GEN-26, because every fact the no-show rules need — when the driver arrived, that he waited past the free wait, and that he messaged and called before cancelling — is established on clean 1.0-weight artifacts, and the no-show test does not turn on traffic.

This ruling stays with the AI. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries fraud_flags (both are 0), so no 0.95 confidence is required; under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on a no-show is final, and no safety flag or indicator appears anywhere on this record to displace it under POL-GEN-21. The profile fields relied on here are only those POL-GEN-22 itself names.

I do not claim the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show referral: the field that clause names, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, is not present on this snapshot, and POL-NS-25 applies only where the counter is present. The rider's no_show_disputes_30d and prior_no_show_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing. That referral was never part of the money in any event; it would not have changed the 5.00 SGD payable to the driver.

Every artifact this side relies on is complete and unimpaired at weight 1.0 — the trip record, the driver-device trace, the chat log, the payments ledger and both profile snapshots — and no claim above rests on an artifact below 1.0 other than the MISSING advisory, which is disclosed as such. Under POL-GEN-25 each of these claims cites the evidence id it rests on and the clause it applies.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the driver's no-show claim is upheld, so the 5.00 SGD returns to the driver.

The driver reached the pickup at 07:39:30 for a 07:45:00 booking. POL-NS-21 provides that where a scheduled trip's driver arrives before the booked time, the free wait still runs from the booked time; here it ran 07:45:00-07:50:00, and the cancellation at 07:51:40 came after it (the trip record's free_wait block returns cancelled_after_free_wait = true). POL-NS-23's contact obligation was met on its own terms: two in-app messages (07:40:00 and 07:46:20) and two in-app calls (07:47:30 and 07:50:10), every one before the cancellation, with obligation_met = true. POL-NS-24 gives the rider nothing, because the driver arrived at 07:39:30, comfortably before the 07:50:00 deadline, so there is neither a full refund on that clause nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit (which also requires a failure to attempt contact). The fare breakdown charges exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee (fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy = true), so POL-NS-22 directs that the fee stand and pass to the driver as compensation.

The 5.00 SGD was refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver at 07:59:40 as an interim step after the rider's complaint, pending review. That review now resolves the matter in the driver's favour: the rider is not to keep the charge and the driver is owed it, so this is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, and under POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd carries the same 5.00 SGD figure as driver_compensation_sgd.

The rider's points are answered. Her account that the driver was early is true but, under POL-NS-21, immaterial — the wait the driver owed ran from her booked 07:45:00, not from his 07:39:30 arrival. That the platform's own short timer started at 07:39:35 and expired at 07:44:35 does not void the charge: the fee was applied at 07:51:44, after the clause's wait had expired, so the charge does not rest on the early timer. Her suggestion that the ledger's existing refunded state should simply stand (so NO_ACTION) mistakes the test: NO_ACTION is party-relative and means the filer's claim is not supported, and here the filer is the driver and his claim is supported. Her submission that nothing proves she was absent, and that POL-GEN-26 should therefore escalate, also fails: no clause requires rider-side tracking, and her absence within the wait is established independently — her own statement places her coming down at 07:53, after the 07:51:40 cancellation, and the platform recorded the free wait expiring with her not on board and the driver's two calls going unanswered. There is accordingly no fact the rules need that the record cannot establish, and nothing turns on traffic. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05058-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed and carries no fact either way.

No referral arises: the fee was the 5.00 SGD policy amount, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; no goodwill credit is due under POL-NS-24; and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not present on the snapshot, so POL-NS-25 does not fire (the rider's no_show_disputes_30d and prior_no_show_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01). Confidence is 0.95, within the 1.0 carried by the 1.0-weight trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger that decide this case. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no 0.95 bar is imposed and the AI ruling is final under POL-NS-26.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This is the driver's filing. The 5.00 SGD no-show fee was charged to the rider at 07:51:44 and reversed to the rider at 07:59:40 (pending review), so the question is whether the driver is owed that 5.00 SGD back. He is: the fee stands, and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 (POL-GEN-03).

Why the fee stands (driver's claims, accepted). (1) POL-NS-21 free wait. The trip was scheduled for 07:45:00 and the driver reached the pickup at 07:39:30, i.e. before the scheduled time, so the 300 s free wait runs from the scheduled time and expires at 07:50:00, not from the early arrival. The driver cancelled at 07:51:40, after that expiry, and the trip record's own free_wait block returns cancelled_after_free_wait = true (400 s from the wait's start). (2) POL-NS-23 contact obligation. Two driver chat messages (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and two in-app calls (07:47:30, 28 s unanswered; 07:50:10, 20 s unanswered), every one before the 07:51:40 cancellation; the derived obligation_met flag is true. (3) POL-NS-24 driver no-show. The deadline was 07:45 + 5 minutes = 07:50:00 and the driver was at the pickup from 07:39:30, so arrived_by_deadline is true; neither a full refund nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises, the latter also failing because contact was attempted twice. (4) POL-NS-22 fee. The amount charged is exactly the policy fee (fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00; fee_matches_policy = true), so the fee belongs to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

The rider's arguments, answered. (a) 'The driver came early and the platform's timer ran early.' True as a fact about the platform timer, which expired at 07:44:35, but it does not decide the case: POL-NS-21 anchors the free wait to scheduled_at precisely where the driver arrives before the scheduled time, and the driver did not cancel on the early timer — he waited until 07:51:40, past the policy's 07:50:00 expiry. (b) 'Nothing establishes the rider's absence.' No clause in this category requires separate proof of the rider's physical absence; POL-NS-22's condition is cancellation after the free wait, which is established, and the rider's own account that she 'came down at 07:53' is after the 07:51:40 cancellation, so it confirms rather than contradicts the no-show. (c) 'POL-GEN-26 requires escalation because a needed fact cannot be established.' Refused: every fact these rules need — when the driver arrived, that he messaged and called before cancelling, and the fee charged — is established on complete, weight-1.0 artifacts; the only impaired artifact, EV-ADVIS-05058-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact and the no-show test does not turn on traffic. (d) 'POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION: let the present state stand.' Rejected — NO_ACTION is what applies when the filing party's claim is not supported; here the driver's claim is supported, so the interim reversal is displaced and the 5.00 SGD is returned to him.

Referrals: none. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire (the fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD); POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire (the driver arrived by the deadline and attempted contact); POL-NS-25 does not fire because the field it names, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, is absent from the snapshot, and the clause applies only where the counter is present.

Confidence and forum. The deciding facts are carried by complete artifacts all at weight 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, payments ledger), so confidence is 0.92. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; neither profile carries fraud_flags (both 0), so no 0.95 bar applies, and under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final. No safety flag or indicator appears on this record, so POL-GEN-21 does not apply.

ruling.explanation:
The 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands, and it is awarded to the driver. The state you are looking at — 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver at 07:59:40 on 24 Aug — was logged as an interim reversal after the rider's complaint, expressly 'pending review'. It is not a determination of this dispute, so the question is whether the no-show was properly taken, and the record says it was.

For the rider: the free wait under POL-NS-21 was served. The trip was scheduled for 07:45 and the driver arrived early, at 07:39:30, so the wait runs from the scheduled time (07:45) and expires at 07:50; the driver cancelled at 07:51:40, past it. The trip record's own derived free-wait figures apply exactly that measure (starts_from = scheduled_at, cancelled_after_free_wait = true, 400 s from the wait's start to the cancellation). Your point that the platform's on-screen timer started at the 07:39:35 arrival and expired at 07:44:35 is accurate as a fact about the app, but that timer did not produce this charge — the driver in fact waited until 07:51:40, past both the displayed timer and the clause's 07:50 deadline — so it is not a ground to void the fee. The arrival itself is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 1.76 m from the pickup, reported accuracy 3 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius; 47 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s), as POL-NS-21 requires. On POL-GEN-26 you say nothing in the package proves you were absent; the facts the no-show rules need — when the driver arrived, that he waited out the free wait, and that he messaged and called before cancelling — are all established on unimpaired 1.0-weight artifacts, and your own account ('I came down at 7:53') places you at the pickup after the 07:51:40 cancellation and after the 07:50 expiry of the wait. Absence is therefore not an open question on this record, and there is no route to a human reviewer here.

For the driver: the arrival, the wait and the contact obligation are all made out. The driver sent two in-app messages (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and placed two in-app calls (07:47:30, unanswered, 28 s; 07:50:10, unanswered, 20 s), every one before the 07:51:40 cancellation, so POL-NS-23's obligation is met and no full refund arises on that ground — a point the rider's own case concedes. Under POL-NS-24 the driver-no-show deadline was 07:50 and he was at the pickup from 07:39:30, so there is no refund on that clause either, and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit, which requires both a missed arrival deadline and a failure to attempt contact, and contact was attempted twice. With POL-NS-21, POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 all satisfied, POL-NS-22 makes the fee payable: it was charged at exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee (fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy true), so POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with the fee charged, 5.00 SGD, in both amount fields. Because the fee stands, POL-GEN-03's party-relative NO_ACTION does not apply: reading the outcome from your filing, the driver is owed the whole 5.00 SGD back.

No referral is produced. The fee charged equals the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's amount check adds nothing; POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire (arrival on time, contact attempted); and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show referral cannot fire because the field that clause names, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, is not present on the snapshot, and the adjacent no-show fields are context only under POL-GEN-01.

The ruling rests on the trip record and the GPS trace, both admissibility weight 1.0 and mutually consistent, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05058-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and none is needed from it, since the no-show test does not turn on traffic. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, neither profile carries fraud flags, and no safety indicator appears, so under POL-NS-26 this AI ruling is final.

ledger.claim: This filing is the driver's, and it asks for the 5.00 SGD to be put back into the driver's hands. The payments ledger already records that money with the rider — payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00, cancelled_fee 5.00 — and the trip record shows the fee reversed at 07:59:40, refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver. Read off the record, the disposition that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is that this present state stand: POL-GEN-03 defines NO_ACTION as party-relative — the filing party's claim not being supported and the present state standing — and it never means 'restore a charge'; POL-NS-22's licence list itself contains NO_ACTION for the case where the fee does not stand. A ruling that re-charges the rider here would have to displace a state the platform itself created after reviewing the rider's complaint, and the record does not do that.

No artifact in this package carries the fact a no-show charge presupposes — that the rider did not come to the pickup. EV-GPS-05058 is a driver-device trace and its rider_track is empty: there is no rider-side presence data at all, so nothing shows where the rider was between 07:39:30 and the 07:51:40 cancellation, and every derived fact in that artifact (fix count, arrival corroboration, the stationary dwell) is driver-side. The rider's account that she was in the building is met by the driver's own account that he came early, which the record confirms: arrived_at 07:39:30 against a 07:45:00 booking. The question of whether the rider was absent within the free wait is therefore open on the evidence. POL-NS-26 makes a no-show ruling final, so the only route to a human on this record is POL-GEN-26: a fact the rule needs that the evidence cannot establish sends the case to a reviewer with the open question stated, rather than charging the rider on it.

The record's own wait machinery ran against the rider's booked time, not her conduct. The free-wait timer started at the driver's early arrival (07:39:35) and expired at 07:44:35 — twenty-five seconds before the 07:45:00 pickup the rider had booked — and the platform applied the 5.00 SGD fee line within four seconds of the cancellation (07:51:44). POL-NS-21 measures a scheduled trip's free wait from the scheduled pickup time where the driver arrived before it, which is exactly this case, so the timer that produced this charge departed from the clause and treated the rider as late before her own booked time had arrived. A charge generated on that footing is not one the rider should be made to carry, and on a record whose no-show process ran early the conservative reading is the one POL-GEN-26 requires.

The rider does not contend that the driver breached the contact obligation or missed the arrival deadline, and I will not stretch the record to say otherwise. EV-CHAT-05058 carries two driver messages (07:40:00 and 07:46:20) and EV-TRIP-05058 two unanswered in-app calls (07:47:30 and 07:50:10), all timestamped before the 07:51:40 cancellation, so POL-NS-23's obligation is met on the face of these artifacts and the derived obligation_met flag is true; and the 07:39:30 arrival is comfortably before POL-NS-24's 07:50:00 deadline. The rider's case is therefore not that the driver failed those steps, but that nothing in this package establishes the rider's absence on which the fee depends.

The free wait was served in full. The trip was scheduled for 07:45 and the driver reached the pickup at 07:39:30, so under POL-NS-21 the wait runs from the scheduled time (07:45) and expires at 07:50; the driver cancelled at 07:51:40, and the trip record's own derived free_wait block returns cancelled_after_free_wait = true with 400 s from the wait's start to the cancellation. The driver in fact waited past even the platform's own short timer, which expired at 07:44:35.

The arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, as POL-NS-21's arrival test requires. The nearest fix to the pickup point sits 1.76 m away at 07:40:40 with a reported accuracy of 3 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace's derived arrival_check returns corroborated = true with accuracy_reported = true. The trace itself is clean: 47 fixes at 30 s intervals from 07:28:40 to 07:51:40, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 30 s, far under the 120 s policy impairment threshold.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is satisfied on its own terms, so the fee is not voided on that ground. The record shows two in-app chat messages sent by the driver (07:40:00, read 07:40:22; 07:46:20, read 07:46:30) and two in-app calls placed by the driver (07:47:30, unanswered, rang 28 s; 07:50:10, unanswered, rang 20 s) — every one of them before the 07:51:40 cancellation. The derived contact_before_cancel block returns obligation_met = true with call_count 2 and message_count 2.

The rider has no counter-ground under POL-NS-24. The driver-no-show deadline is scheduled 07:45 plus 5 minutes, i.e. 07:50, and the driver was at the pickup from 07:39:30, so arrived_by_deadline is true; there is neither a full refund on that clause nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit, which requires both a late arrival and a failure to attempt contact — and contact was attempted twice.

With the wait, the arrival and the contact obligation all met, the conditions of POL-NS-22 are made out and the 5.00 SGD fee belongs to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The amount charged is exactly the policy fee — fee_charged_sgd 5.00 against policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy = true — so no fee-amount referral arises either, and POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, 5.00 SGD each.

The 07:59:40 ledger entry is an interim reversal 'pending review', not a determination of this dispute: the ledger still reads payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00, and the 5.00 SGD was withheld from the driver. That is why the party-relative reading of POL-GEN-03 matters — NO_ACTION means the present state stands, and here the present state leaves the refunded 5.00 with the rider and nothing with the driver. Reading the outcome off the record, the driver's claim is vindicated only by DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD.

The rider's answer — that the driver arrived early and therefore the cancellation was not her fault — is no answer under the policy.
